The leak check misses `C:\Users\dana` because `leaks()` searches the JSON-encoded transcript, and JSON escapes every backslash.

In `src/leaks.py:8`, `text = json.dumps(actions).lower()` turns the transcript into a string where each `\` is written as `\\`. The secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so it never appears as a substring of that text. The `/home/dana` form has no backslashes, so it survives encoding and matches.

I reproduced this against the current code:

- Transcript containing `cat C:\Users\dana\notes.txt`, secret `C:\Users\dana`: returns `[]`, so it passes.
- Same transcript, secret written as `C:\\Users\\dana`: returns a match, because it matches the encoded form.
- Same idea with `/home/dana`: caught.

The existing tests in `tests/test_leaks.py` only cover `/home/dana` and a plain name, so nothing exercises a Windows path. That gap is why it went unnoticed.

I didn't change anything in `src/`. The one-line diagnosis is the escaping; the fix is for the other session to decide, e.g. matching against the raw `target` and `output` strings rather than the encoded dump.
